clue.text: Backing church that's prevalent around South American city

indicators.note: the word for prevalent goes round the turned church abbreviation

parts.note: something rife is widespread or prevalent

indicators.note: backing tells you the church abbreviation is written from its far end to its start

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Supporting a church that is widespread near a city in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like supporting, but it turns the church abbreviation round before 'around' wraps the word for prevalent about it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a large port on the Atlantic coast of Brazil.

clue.text: Entertaining king and queen, celebs revealing all

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside, so the celebs hold the two royals

parts.note: celebrities are stars
K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Celebrities who host royalty spill every secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' is the container signal, not hospitality. The answer is British slang for stark naked, so 'revealing all' is meant bodily, not as gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang synonym: someone completely naked is showing everything.

clue.text: Old traveller takes moment to pen line before game

indicators.note: before places the first assembled part ahead of the game
to pen is to enclose, so the moment encloses the line

parts.note: a mo is a short moment, as in 'half a mo'
an arc is a curved line
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: An elderly tourist pauses to write a sentence before a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pen' looks like writing but means enclosing, and 'before' sets that part ahead of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the famous medieval Venetian explorer who journeyed to China.

clue.text: Noble of a couple to welcome principal of college

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the word for twofold takes in a letter

parts.note: dual means of two, belonging to a pair

indicators.note: the principal is the head, so the head letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An aristocratic pair greet the head of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to welcome' puts C, picked by 'principal of', inside DUAL. 'Noble' is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjectival synonym: relating to a duke, a high rank of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Twisted acts, deep down

indicators.note: twisted round, so the word for acts is read from its end to its start

parts.note: acts of Parliament are laws
a deep voice or note is a low one

explanation.surface: Perverse deeds, buried far beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' turns LAWS into SWAL; only that piece is turned. 'down' is a verb, as in downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to gulp a drink is to knock it back.

clue.text: Batter served with alcoholic drink, coarse stuff

indicators.note: served with sets the two pieces side by side, the drink first

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or any alcoholic drink
to batter something is to ram it

explanation.surface: Fried food in batter comes with a beer, all rather rough fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' is a verb, to strike, not the coating for fish. 'stuff' is an old word for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a rough fabric of silk and mohair, and stuff means cloth.

clue.text: Game German cyclist passing right-angled bend

indicators.note: passing the bend means coming after it, so the German follows the letter

parts.note: a pipe or road bend at a right angle is an L, from the letter's shape
Nikolaus Otto was the German engineer who devised the Otto cycle of the four-stroke engine

explanation.surface: A plucky German rider rounds a sharp corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cyclist' is a joke: Otto gave his name to the engine cycle, not to bike racing. 'passing' puts him after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a numbers lottery, a contest of chance.

clue.text: Whole play includes introductions to twelve audio books

indicators.note: includes tells you the word for play has the other pieces within it

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

indicators.note: introductions are openings, so the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: lit is short for literature, books collectively

explanation.surface: The complete drama comes with the opening parts of a dozen audiobooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is a verb, to trifle, not a drama; 'includes' and 'introductions to' do the building. 'Whole' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun synonym: the entirety of something.

clue.text: Approximately 167ft European plant

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals, and 51 metres is about 167 feet

explanation.surface: A continental factory roughly 167 feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: Convert 167 feet to 51 metres and write the number in Roman numerals. 'plant' suggests a factory, not something growing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: the linden, a tall growing thing.

clue.text: Step one of twelve

definitions.meaning: to step out in time, as soldiers do on parade
one of the twelve months of the year

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a soldier's regular walking pace and the third month.

clue.text: Strangely, I do fast food from Greece

indicators.note: in a strange way, so the letters that follow are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Oddly, the speaker cooks quick Greek meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges I, DO and FAST. 'fast' is letters only, not a kind of meal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Greek beef and onion casserole.

clue.text: Presents to send a criminal

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters before it are disarranged

explanation.surface: Gifts to post to a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges TO, SEND and A. 'Presents' is a verb here, not gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: gives something freely.

clue.text: At home, opening letter from abroad to find money

indicators.note: the word for at home opens up the foreign letter, splitting it and sitting inside

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Indoors, someone slits an overseas envelope and discovers cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' is a verb of splitting apart, not an envelope being slit, and the letter belongs to the Greek alphabet rather than the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang synonym for cash.

clue.text: Hardship carrying on thus describing Figaro's work, perhaps?

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the word for hardship holds the other two pieces

parts.note: a trial is an ordeal or hardship
taken as written
so means thus

explanation.surface: Difficulty keeps going like this, summing up an opera composer's labours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is the container signal. Figaro is the Barber of Seville, so his work is cutting hair, not Mozart's or Rossini's music.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective meaning relating to a barber, which is Figaro's trade.

clue.text: Brilliant starter of tortiglioni cooked so as to be firm, daughter left till last

indicators.note: the starter is what comes first, so the first letter of the next word is taken
left till last means this letter is taken from its place and set at the very end

parts.words: cooked so as to be firm
parts.note: al dente is the Italian term for pasta cooked firm to the bite
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A superb pasta first course cooked firm, the daughter being served after everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter of' takes T; 'left till last' shifts the D of AL DENTE to the end, giving ALENTE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: highly gifted.

clue.text: US city refurbished ancient craft

parts.note: something refurbished is made as new
Noah's ark is a vessel of ancient times

explanation.surface: An American town has revived an old handicraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' is a boat, not a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: the largest place in New Jersey.

clue.text: Bank accepting failure in careless style

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for bank takes in the word for failure

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a miss is a failure to hit

explanation.surface: A lender slackly tolerates a default.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is a verb, to depend, not a lender, and 'accepting' makes it take in the word for failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb synonym: negligently.

clue.text: Natural flow, we hear? One's dried up

indicators.note: we hear tells you the word for a flow is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a current is the natural flow of water or air

explanation.surface: A stream is reported, but it has run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals a word that sounds like CURRENT. 'dried up' describes fruit, not a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small dried grape.

clue.text: Free to travel, pay hike ultimately squeezing ladies and gentlemen

indicators.note: squeezing means gripping from both sides, so the first two pieces hold the third between them

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the ladies and the gents are loos, British for public toilets

explanation.surface: No fares, since a wage rise in the end puts pressure on the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezing' and 'ultimately' do the building. Ladies and Gentlemen are the signs on British public toilets, not an audience being addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unattached and able to roam at will.

clue.text: While putting one's foot down, showing uncanny perception?

parts.note: while can mean though, as in 'while I agree, ...'
treading is literally setting a foot on the ground

explanation.surface: Someone insists firmly yet displays eerie insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting one's foot down' is meant literally, a step, not being firm.
explanation.definitionFit: It is telepathy, knowing what is in another's mind.

clue.text: Ballet depended on love

parts.note: something that rode on an outcome depended on it
love is a score of nothing in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A dance company relied on affection.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: Aaron Copland's 1942 cowboy dance work.

clue.text: Preserving earliest part of railway, save a few lines?

indicators.note: preserving means keeping within, so the word for save keeps a letter inside it

parts.note: save means except, as in 'all save one'

indicators.note: the earliest part of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Campaigners protect the oldest stretch of track and rescue some branch routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserving' puts R, from 'earliest part of', inside EXCEPT. 'save' is a preposition and the lines are of text, not track.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a short passage taken from a longer text.

clue.text: Game stew containing a meat product

indicators.note: containing tells you the stew has the single letter within it

parts.note: a salmi is a rich stew of game birds

explanation.surface: A casserole of venison with sausage in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts A inside SALMI, a ragout of game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a cured Italian sausage.

clue.text: Comforter imparting courage after trouble

indicators.note: after places the word for courage behind the phrase for trouble

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in trouble
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: A friend who consoles gives you nerve once the crisis is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' orders the pieces. BOTTLE is British slang for nerve, as in 'losing your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a rubber container filled to warm a bed, a source of comfort.

clue.text: Fish something worthless on its own?

parts.note: a lemon is slang for a dud, a useless thing
sole means single, alone

explanation.surface: Angling for a thing of no value by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a European flatfish.

clue.text: After small pot, most fancy a kebab

indicators.note: after tells you the shortened word for fancy follows the small pot

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
pot and hash are both slang for cannabis

indicators.note: most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it

explanation.surface: Following a little cannabis, nearly everyone wants a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is cannabis, not a pan. 'most' trims the final letter from the word for fancy, and 'After' sets what remains behind the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: It is skewered grilled meat from the Caucasus.

clue.text: First Latin one repeated in translation

indicators.note: translation is a carrying across, so the letters are rendered into a new order
repeated tells you the letter for one is used twice

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The opening Roman numeral said again when the text is rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' gives I twice, and 'in translation' rearranges LATIN with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: occurring at the beginning.

clue.text: Drink container topped up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom to the top
topped means the head is cut off, removing the first letter

parts.note: a canister is a container for tea or gas

explanation.surface: Someone refills a glass to the brim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes the C of CANISTER, leaving ANISTER, and 'up' reads that from the bottom. 'topped up' looks like one phrase but is two instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a Greek wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Quick wit in an abnormal sense slowing

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, a sense beyond the normal five
rit is the musical abbreviation for ritardando, slowing down

explanation.surface: A sharp mind is, oddly, losing speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slowing' is the musical marking rit., short for ritardando.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym from French: liveliness of mind.

clue.text: Hard growth beneath a nut

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath places the hard growth under the single letter

parts.note: a corn is a patch of hardened skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A tough lump is found underneath a seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beneath' puts CORN under the A in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fruit of the oak.
